claims.text: AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock is intended for additive manufacturing of miniature components.
Adaptive LPBF scanning can dynamically modulate laser power, scan speed, and scan pattern to control local solidification cooling rates.
LPBF processing strategies can program the evolution of an alloy's microstructure.
Adaptive thermal scanning will moderate thermal gradients during solidification.
Modulating cooling rates and thermal gradients alters nucleation and grain-growth kinetics.
The altered solidification kinetics will produce finer, more equiaxed grains with reduced columnarity in AlCrFeNiSi.
A refined, more equiaxed grain structure will lower residual stress at grain boundaries.
Refining the grain structure will reduce residual thermal stresses in miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
Refining the grain structure will improve yield strength and hardness.
Adaptive-scanned components will have lower residual thermal stresses than components produced by conventional high-thermal-load LPBF.
Adaptive-scanned components will have higher yield strength and hardness than components produced by conventional high-thermal-load LPBF.
Conventional high-thermal-load LPBF typically produces coarse microstructures.
Conventional high-thermal-load LPBF typically produces elevated residual stresses.
Conventional high-thermal-load LPBF typically degrades mechanical properties.
A processing window that limits peak temperatures and thermal gradients is applicable to miniature AlCrFeNiSi geometries.
The adaptive strategy is expected to be most effective for miniature AlCrFeNiSi components, while its efficacy for larger geometries or other alloys is unestablished.
Prior observations in similar systems support the expected microstructural refinement and corresponding mechanical improvements.
